title: The simplest constraint forcing a non-repetitive pattern forces a nested one

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The simplest constraint forcing a non-repetitive pattern forces a nested one

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Among 2D template constraints that also require one template to appear somewhere, systematic search over more than 18 million constraints finds that the first constraint forcing a non-repetitive pattern (number 18762389) forces a unique nested pattern.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: after examining more than 18 million of them, one finally discovers the system shown on the facing page. And in this system, unlike all others before it, no repetitive pattern is possible; the only pattern that satisfies the constraint is the non-repetitive nested pattern shown in the picture.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 5, “Two Dimensions and Beyond”; section “Systems Based on Constraints” (from p. 210), p. 218. Scope: two-dimensional template constraints with a required-template condition

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch05-18: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.80

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The finite ordering and exact system make the claim sharply testable. The specific system can be checked, but independently establishing “first,” uniqueness, and forced nesting requires substantial exhaustive computation plus formal reasoning.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct the exact ordering of required-template constraints, verify that system 18762389 has a unique satisfying orbit with nested structure, and exhaustively check every preceding system for a periodic solution. A prior aperiodic system or an alternative solution refutes the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Uniqueness over an infinite plane may require a proof.

Exhaustive search is substantial.

The numbering and equivalence conventions require reconstruction.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.93
data existence: 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Constraint 18762389 is explicitly described, and its nested coloring can be checked against the twelve templates in weeks. The claim also says it is the first such constraint after more than 18 million trials and that the coloring is the only one, which is a large search plus an infinite-grid uniqueness argument. Public material settles the single picture much more readily than the priority and uniqueness clauses.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct the book's numbering, force constraint 18762389 from its required template, and test whether the resulting coloring is the published base-2 nested pattern and whether any earlier constraint already has no repetitive solution. An earlier aperiodic example, or a second infinite coloring, would refute the corresponding clause.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Uniqueness on the infinite grid needs a forcing argument, not only a finite picture.

Showing this constraint is first requires the same standard on more than 18 million predecessors.

The numbering scheme has to be reconstructed before the index can be audited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.72
analysis feasibility: 0.42
operationalizability: 0.78
